record.provider: Notion (free plan) - file blocks & Files property

free_tier.stated: No total storage cap: 'Unlimited file uploads' on Free, but each file is capped at 5 MiB on Free (5 GiB on paid). Block limit is unlimited for a single-member Free workspace.

egress.terms: Free; Notion serves via S3/presigned URLs on Cloudflare-fronted notion.com. File objects return 'An authenticated HTTP GET URL... valid for one hour', so links must be re-minted - no CDN you can pin a cache to without re-signing.

record.tooling: Official Notion API file-upload endpoints (single-part <=20 MiB, multi-part above with 5-20 MiB parts) + PlakarKorp/integration-notion and many notion-backup repos for bulk extraction; no rclone backend
record.chaining: Per-record unlimited: 5 MiB per file across unlimited files, blocks, and free workspaces. Sharding large datasets into 5 MiB objects requires approximately 200,000 objects per terabyte at the 600 requests per minute API rate limit.
record.limits_note: 5 MiB per file on Free (hard, enforced by API); 20 MiB per single-part API upload; parts must be 5-20 MiB; 600 requests/min per workspace (avg 10/s) shared across all connections; only whitelisted MIME types (audio/document/image/video/CAD) - arbitrary binary is rejected
record.reliability_note: The MIME whitelist is the killer: no generic octet-stream blobs, so archival datasets must be packed as .zip/.7z/.tar which Notion does accept. Signed URLs expire in one hour, so serving 1 TB/day out of Notion means re-minting continuously.

evidence.proved: 'Free workspaces are limited to 5 MiB (binary megabytes) per file'; 'Files larger than 20 MiB must be split into parts'; supported-types table lists .zip, .7z, .tar, .bz2, .rar
'Unlimited file uploads'; 'On the Free plan, you can upload images, videos and file attachments up to 5MB each. Upgrade to a paid plan for unlimited file uploads with a ~5GB max per file.'
'An authenticated HTTP GET URL to the file. The URL is valid for one hour.'
